What Are Common Problems Affecting Indoor Air Quality?

There are quite a few problems affecting the indoor air quality of your home. They can cause allergies to flare up, uncomfortable breathing, and even health problems. Here are some of the more common issues that can be found:

items: Allergens: Things such as dust, pet dander, and pollen can create an unpleasant breathing environment in your home.
Bacteria and mold: A buildup of bacteria and mold in your home’s air can result in some serious health issues if left ignored.
Stale air: Breathing stale air may get uncomfortable after some time. It may also aid unwanted odors in sticking around longer.
Household chemicals: From your cleaning products to the paint on the walls to the aerosol products you use, every home is loaded with chemicals that can affect air quality.

Should You Consider a Dehumidifier For Your Home?

A dehumidifier is a device that removes humidity from the air. It works by drawing in air then regulating it to a certain temperature below the dew point. After the humidity is released into a trap, the clean air is put back into circulation. It takes, removes, and then gives back.
It’s also important to know what kind of air filter your home uses and if your air filter can be recycled or not.

Excessive humidity in the air can cause many problems ranging from odors to creating a food supply for bacteria and mold. By eliminating the source, you will find a solution. Not only is the air safer to breathe when you add a dehumidifier, it also becomes more comfortable.
